item.title: Tunable first-order transitions and magnetic hysteresis in Bernal pentalayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.31376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior, as a displacement field can shift the energy difference between subbands. Here, we demonstrate this principle in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene, whose low-energy spectrum comprises a monolayer-like Dirac sub-band together with light and heavy bilayer-like sub-bands. Local compressibility measurements resolve a fully symmetry-broken Landau-level spectrum and a sequence of phase transitions that occur when Landau levels of different subbands cross, at which strong interactions redistribute the occupation among flavors. We show that these transitions exhibit hysteretic Hall responses in magnetic field, confirming their first-order character, and that the magnitude and sign of the hysteresis are tuned by the displacement field, as expected from the subband Landau-level ordering determined in compressibility measurements. Our work establishes the subband degree of freedom in multiband systems as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching, and highlights how local thermodynamic measurements can link microscopic insights to macroscopic responses in quantum materials.
item.dc:creator: Wentian Zheng, Jiawei Hu, Yuxuan Yao, Fang Xie, Zihan Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Qimiao Si, Yonglong Xie

item.title: Moir\'e-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.31423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moir\'e bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moir\'e bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.
item.dc:creator: Bogdan Borodin, Xuanpu Zhang, Christopher Yang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Cyprian Lewandowski, Petr Stepanov

item.title: Excess noise and electron-phonon energy transfer in Au wires: Length and temperature effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.31519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As a mesoscopic diffusive wire at low temperatures is driven out of equilibrium by a current, excess noise is observed compared to the equilibrium Johnson-Nyquist fluctuations. The expected form of the excess noise varies depending on the relative rates of wire traversal, electron-electron inelastic energy transfer, and electron-phonon inelastic energy transfer. We measure noise as a function of bias current in diffusive Au nanowires on SiO2/Si with lengths ranging from sub-{\mu}m to 30 {\mu}m and temperatures from 3 K to 50 K, to map out the interplay between charge shot noise and the crossover to electron self-heating and phonon-dominated noise suppression. As expected qualitatively, shot noise is suppressed with increasing wire length and substrate temperature, as electron-phonon scattering is of increasing importance. In long wires, the simple model of electron-phonon energy loss known to be quantitatively effective below a few Kelvin underpredicts the excess noise in the high bias, high temperature limit. This issue is more severe in wires on SiO2/Si than on bare Si, implying that interfacial thermal conduction must be considered in the thermal path even at comparatively high temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Yuxin Wan, Dale T. Lowder, Liyang Chen, Manasi Mandal, Gavin Joyce, Douglas Natelson

item.title: Interface and film engineering for improved spin-charge interconversion in sputtered GeTe nanodevices
item.description: arXiv:2611.31816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-logic devices promise non-volatile logic-in-memory computing with ultra-low power consumption, offering a route to circumvent the von Neumann bottleneck. Magnetoelectric and ferroelectric spin-orbit (MESO/FESO) devices, however, require spin-charge interconversion materials that combine a large output signal with properties that survive nanoscale integration. Tellurides are particularly fragile in this respect, as processing readily introduces defects that degrade their spin-charge interconversion properties. Here we demonstrate room-temperature spin-charge interconversion in patterned FESO nanoscale devices based on sputtered GeTe, with feature sizes down to 100 nm. By introducing a Ti interfacial layer between the CoFe electrode and GeTe, and by using GeTe films of improved crystalline quality, we increase the interconversion output signal from 3 m{\Omega} to 24 m{\Omega}, exceeding values reported for platinum at comparable device size. These results establish large-scale-deposited GeTe as a viable material platform for spin-logic devices and identify interface quality and film crystallinity as key levers for optimizing their performance.

item.title: Moir\'e-Induced Interlayer Electron-Phonon Coupling in Graphene/hBN Superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.31896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moir\'e superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moir\'e potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moir\'e electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moir\'e superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moir\'e flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moir\'e electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Dasol Kim, Zhengguang Lu, Tonghang Han, Guorui Chen, Tianyi Han, Jixiang Yang, Bing Cheng, Zhenxian Liu, Christopher Homes, G. L. Carr, Jeong Min Park, Qihang Zhang, Lili Jiang, Hongyuan Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Feng Wang, Long Ju

item.title: Environmentally assisted transport in a diamond chain
item.description: arXiv:2611.32027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quantum transport in a diamond chain coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its boundaries. The system is subject to uniform dephasing and an external magnetic field threading a flux $\Phi$ per plaquette. We derive exact analytical solutions for $\Phi=0$ and $\Phi=\pi$. We show that in the all-bands-flat regime at $\Phi=\pi$, dephasing destroys Aharonov-Bohm caging, leading to environment-assisted quantum transport. Our results demonstrate that coupling a flat-band system to a dissipative environment provides a viable route for controlling transport in regimes where coherent dynamics alone would result in complete localization.
item.dc:creator: Pavel S. Muraev, Andrey R. Kolovsky, Dmitrii N. Maksimov

item.title: Towards determination of intrinsic spin properties in MAPbI$_3$ crystals using spin noise spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.32115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin noise spectroscopy in back- and forward-scattering geometries is used to study the spin dynamics of charge carriers in a MAPbI$_3$ (MA = methylammonium) single crystal. The spectra reveal electrons and holes with different degrees of localization. At low temperatures ($T \approx 4$~K), hole spin relaxation is dominated by the hyperfine interaction with nuclear spins. The broadening of the spectra with increasing temperature can be attributed to thermally activated hopping of localized holes. From the thermal activation energies, we estimate hole localization lengths that are consistent with both the hyperfine-induced dephasing rates and the zero-field frequency shifts measured at low temperature. By contrast, the electron spin dynamics cannot be explained by the hyperfine interaction alone: even at the lowest excitation powers, it is affected by the probe light, and we observe a slowing down of spin relaxation with increasing power. Comparison of the back- and forward-scattered spin noise signals indicates that the spatial distribution of carriers is inhomogeneous: electrons are located preferentially near the crystal surface, weakly localized holes (characterized by slower spin relaxation) are found mostly away from the surface, and strongly localized holes are somewhere in between.
item.dc:creator: M. Vladimirova, S. Cronenberger, L. Doyenette, D. R. Yakovlev, B. Turedi, M. V. Kovalenko

item.title: Topological Narrow Bands in Twisted Rhombohedral Multilayer Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.32229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e graphene multilayers provide an atomically thin platform for engineering narrow topological bands through stacking, twist, and electrostatic control. Recent experiments on twisted rhombohedral graphene have revealed a high-Chern-number hierarchy determined by the number of rhombohedral layers. A microscopic description of this hierarchy requires connecting the ideal chiral picture to the realistic electronic structure. Here, we show that the two central moir\'e bands of twisted monolayer-$N$-layer rhombohedral graphene originate from hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state located at opposite corners of the moir\'e Brillouin zone. Increasing $N$ progressively narrows these bands, whereas reversing the displacement field transfers their wave-function weight between the twisted interface and the remote surface. In spectrally isolated regimes, this redistribution switches the lower band between Chern numbers $\mathcal{C}=N$ and $\mathcal{C}=-1$. A projected surface theory shows how interfacial tunneling is dressed by virtual propagation through the rhombohedral stack, explaining the field-selected Chern hierarchy and the recurring threefold structure of the real-space charge textures. These results establish layer number and displacement field as complementary nanoscale controls of band flatness, spatial polarization, and topology in graphene moir\'e heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Jimeno-Pozo, Danna Liu, Francisco Guinea, Pierre A. Pantale\'on

item.title: Periodic and quasiperiodic structures produced by microphase separation in one-component simple liquids with competing interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Competing interactions can generate frustration which suppresses macroscopic-scale phase separation, superseding it with separation patterns on the microscopic scale. This phenomenon, referred to as microphase separation, produces thermodynamically stable mesoscopic-scale periodic patterns in systems of different physical nature. The studies of this effect follow two paradigms. First, in block copolymers, the macroscopic-scale separation of chemically distinct components is prevented by the covalent bonds between them. In the other, the microscopic-scale separation is produced in simple single-component liquids by the competition between a short-range attraction and a long-range repulsion (SALR) in the pair potential, the separation occurring between a dense phase and a gas. The interest in the simple liquid models with SALR interaction was inspired by the apparent universality of the modulated structures generated by competing interactions in different systems. Simple particle models are tractable by theory and thereby make it possible to discern the microscopic mechanisms of pattern formation; particle-based simulations give access to systems beyond the reach of experiments. In this Perspective we review the recent advances in the molecular-dynamics simulation of microphase separation in single-component simple liquids using SALR potentials. We show that these simulations reproduce the mesophases typical of block copolymers and liquid crystals, which demonstrates that the complexity of the constituent particles of real liquids is not a necessary condition for their formation, and that they produce novel periodic morphologies of both conceptual interest and technological relevance; we discuss how simulated mesophases can serve as templates for metamaterials whose properties are governed by topology.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Agosta, Alfredo Metere, Mikhail Dzugutov

item.title: Angular Momentum Hall Effect of Axial Ferrons in Ferroelectrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.32331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon thermal and angular-momentum (AM) Hall effects are known in non-ferroelectric insulators, yet whether terahertz soft modes of displacive ferroelectrics, i.e., ``ferrons", share them remains open. We report axial ferrons that hold polarization-momentum locking in uniaxial ferroelectrics and show that both effects exist: a longitudinal temperature gradient drives a transverse AM flow without any field, whereas an out-of-plane magnetic field switches on the thermal Hall response. Two competitive channels emerge for the AM Hall effect: self-radiated magnetic fields hybridize two branches into circular modes whose momentum-locked Berry curvature deflects opposite magnetic moments to opposite edges, while temperature-gradient-induced mode quantum coherence adds a magnetic-moment dipole that leads to an opposite transverse AM current. An out-of-plane magnetic field breaks the exact polarization-momentum locking and yields a polarization Hall current. Numerical calculations show these effects are significant in both LiNbO$_3$ and van der Waals ferroelectrics. Edge magnetization or polarization accumulation can switch adjacent magnets or ferroelectrics, enabling low-power magnetoelectric functionality by thermal current in the future.
item.dc:creator: Xiyin Ye, Tao Yu

item.title: Reconfigurable Chiral Phonons and Their Selection in Asymmetrically Stacked Graphene MoirMoir\'{e} Superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.32466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral phonons, lattice vibrations carrying angular momentum, offer a new handle for controlling phonon-mediated phenomena in condensed matter, yet their on-demand generation and deterministic control remain challenging. Here we show, using helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy, that asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices provide a reconfigurable platform for chiral phonons. We observe a finite degree of circular polarization for both chiral interlayer shear phonons and intralayer optical phonons. A chiral-phonon Raman-tensor model attributes this response to interfacial $C_{2}$-symmetry breaking together with Raman resonance within the van Hove singularity region. Reversing either the twist sense or the stacking order inverts the degree of circular polarization through the spatial transformations linking the corresponding stacking geometries. By tuning the excitation energy and twist angle, we achieve nearly full-range control of the degree of circular polarization of interlayer shear phonons, from $-1$ to $1$, while gate-induced interlayer potential redistribution enables substantial and reversible in situ modulation. These results establish asymmetrically stacked graphene moir\'{e} superlattices as a versatile platform for generating and controlling chiral phonons, with implications for optoelectronic and quantum technologies.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Fei Zhang, Ting-Ting Wang, Zhong-Jie Wang, Miao-Ling Lin, Yue Wang, Zi-Jian Zhong, Xue-Lu Liu, Heng Wu, Lin-Shang Chen, Yan-Meng Shi, Jin-Yang Lou, Lin-Han Li, Jia-Liang Xie, Rui Mei, Ti-Ying Zhu, Li-Fa Zhang, Jiang-Bin Wu, Ping-Heng Tan

item.title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the {\pi}-conjugated spacers
item.description: arXiv:2611.32611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nature of the {\pi}-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.
item.dc:creator: Laurette-Apolline Jerro, Imen Hnid, Imane Arbouch, Ali Yassin, David Gu\'erin, Alexis Elias, Colin van Dyck, Lionel Sanguinet, J\'er\^ome Cornil, St\'ephane Lenfant, Philippe Blanchard, Dominique Vuillaume

item.title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the scalar Schr\"odinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|\Omega_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|\Omega_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.
item.dc:creator: Humberto Belich Jr., Edilberto O. Silva

item.title: Intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect in ferroaxial metals with high-order rotation axes
item.description: arXiv:2611.32709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-field Hall resistivity of non-magnetic metals has an intrinsic quantum contribution that derives from the field-corrected Berry curvature and intrinsic magnetic moment of the Bloch states near the Fermi surface. However, its effect is usually overshadowed by the classical Lorentz-force contribution. Here we show that for the longitudinal Hall effect, which occurs in ferroaxial crystals when the applied magnetic field lies in the Hall plane, the Lorentz force contribution vanishes for the eight ferroaxial groups with a 3,4 or 6-fold rotation axis. This provides an opportunity to measure the quantum correction in isolation, but so far all measured instances of the effect fall in the remaining five ferroaxial groups of lower symmetry, where the Lorentz force dominates the signal. We compile a list of candidate ferroaxial metals with such high-order rotation axis and compute the Hall effect from first principles for representative candidates, identifying Ni$_3$P with $\sigma^{\rm H}_{xzx} = 28.4$ S/m/T as a promising material to unambiguously measure the intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect.
item.dc:creator: Eleni Chatzikyriakou, Stepan Tsirkin, Fernando Pe\~naranda, Oscar Pozo, Ivo Souza, Fernando de Juan

item.title: Recovery of Extended Modes from the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Due to Local Nonlinearity on a Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.32783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Localization in continuum spectra known as the non-Hermitian skin effect is widely believed to be a consequence of nontrivial topology of bulk bands. However, the robustness of the non-Hermitian skin effect against nonlinear effects is still a nontrivial problem. We here reveal that single-bond nonlinearity on a boundary can recover extended modes in a non-Hermitian tight-binding model. We propose and analyze a one-dimensional minimal model, where we introduce a nonlinear phase shift of a hopping term only at boundary sites. We also propose a possible photonic setup to dynamically observe the nonlinearity-induced extended modes as a steady state. Our results thus challenge the conventional notion of the non-Hermitian skin effect by revealing its dependence on nonlinear boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Kazuki Sone, Tomonari Mizoguchi, Yasuhiro Hatsugai

item.title: Classification of spin space groups and crystal magnetic orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.33099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin space groups (SSGs) describe magnetic crystals in the limit of negligible spin-orbit coupling, where spatial and spin rotations decouple. Although algebraic enumerations of SSGs exist, their abstract mathematical approaches obscure the physical meaning of the resulting classifications, leaving the direct correspondence between SSGs and real-space magnetic orders unestablished. Here, we present a physically motivated framework for enumerating and classifying SSGs based on their translation holonomy---the image of the spatial lattice translation group under the spin homomorphism. The three classes of abelian images in $SO(3)$ divide SSGs into three basic translation types. Translation holonomy constrains the spin operations associated with point-group elements, yielding a complete enumeration of SSGs organized by a physical hierarchy. Within this framework, translation holonomy classifies SSGs and magnetic orders into 17 universal spin-lattice types, each with unambiguous Bragg-peak geometries and polarization signatures in neutron diffraction. Beyond organizing known magnetic orders, this framework directly predicts four universal physical phenomena: (i) exact magnetization compensation enforced by certain spin-lattice types; (ii) an exact group-theoretic criterion for the emergence of noncommuting Brillouin zones; (iii) a new type of 3Q magnetic order with vanishing octupoles; and (iv) the realization of strictly collinear momentum-space spin textures protected by reflection-staggered coplanar spin lattices. We also construct a spin space group database organized according to this physical hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Zhang, Peiyuan Wang, Y. X. Zhao

item.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.33155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].
item.dc:creator: Aiden Mains, Danile Salib, Christopher Leong, Bitan Roy

item.title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
item.description: arXiv:2611.31383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.
item.dc:creator: Mingyao Guo, Luting Wang, Murali Suganya, Biqiong Yu, Martin Greven, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Raman Sankar, Yao Wang, David Hsieh

item.title: Superconductivity with valley-imbalanced Fermi surfaces in thick rhombohedral graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.31861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superconductivity in spin-polarized metals challenges conventional opposite-spin pairing, particularly when a magnetic field strengthens rather than suppresses it. In graphene, the additional valley degree of freedom broadens the possible pairing channels, making the valley occupation of the parent metal central to understanding such superconductivity. Here we report in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity in hBN-aligned 17-layer rhombohedral graphene. Normal-state quantum oscillations reveal unequal Fermi pockets consistent with a valley-imbalanced, spin-polarized parent metal. Calculations show that the parent electron pocket is predominantly localized on the bottom surface and largely preserved by electrostatic screening as additional Fermi pockets emerge. Superconductivity persists in this regime but is suppressed when carriers are polarized toward the hBN-aligned surface, where the parent bands undergo strong moire reconstruction. An adjacent nonlinear metallic response evolves continuously into superconducting critical-current features and persists above the superconducting transition temperature. The combination of valley imbalance and in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity motivates a phenomenological magnon-assisted equal-spin intervalley pairing scenario. These findings provide experimental constraints on pairing in valley-imbalanced metals and open a route to testing magnetic pairing mechanisms through layer-selective control of the parent electronic states.
item.dc:creator: Le Liu, Jian Zhao, Cheng Xu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yang Zhang, Weibo Gao

item.title: Emergent Electric-Field-Tunable $p$-Wave Magnetism in Twisted Bilayer NiPS$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.32103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A perpendicular electric field can reorient a momentum-space spin texture without changing the local magnetic configuration. In this Letter, we investigate this mechanism in a $21^\circ$-twisted $\mathrm{NiPS}_3$ bilayer with zigzag order and coplanar, nonparallel layer N\'eel vectors. In the ideal nonrelativistic limit, an antiunitary in-plane half-translation enforces opposite-spin pairing at opposite momenta, while a layer-exchanging twofold operation pins the leading $p$-wave spin splitting to a crystallographic direction. A perpendicular layer bias lifts this orientational constraint while preserving the antiunitary symmetry, allowing a transverse component of the splitting vector. First-principles calculations show gate-dependent reorientation and deformation of spin-resolved isoenergy contours. Wannier-based linear-response calculations further reveal field-activated diagonal spin conductivities and a polarity-dependent tilt in the angular profile of the transverse spin-current response. The spin-texture axis, dispersion axes, and transport-response axis are distinct quantities governed by the same symmetry reduction. These results identify layer bias as a route to controlling odd-parity spin textures and spin-current anisotropy, provided that the coplanar magnetic state remains stable.
item.dc:creator: Jiaran Su, Jin-Xin Hu, Qi Sun, Dante M. Kennes, Yuhao Fu, Lede Xian, Lijun Zhang

item.title: Topological terahertz fields from tunable vectorial currents
item.description: arXiv:2611.32586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Future information processing calls for photonic architectures with greater capacity, intrinsic resilience to noise, and direct integration with quantum materials and devices. Topological light pulses have recently emerged as promising candidates to meet these demands, yet the complexity underlying their unique properties also makes them challenging to generate, tune, and fully resolve in space and time. Here, we generate and actively tune topological light fields through transient vectorial currents in an optoelectronic metasurface. Incident linear polarization steers the local direction of photocurrents in graphene via nanoplasmonic resonators with triangular symmetry, while a global winding pattern enables continuous tuning between compressional and circulating charge flows. Under ultrafast excitation, these currents radiate single-cycle terahertz toroidal pulses spanning electric- and magnetic-dominant modes with dynamically evolving skyrmion textures. Full spatiotemporal mapping and reconstruction provide a complete visualization of the toroidal structure of light, directly tracing the closed field surfaces while continuously tracking skyrmion number and helicity throughout a single cycle. These results connect two-dimensional vectorial currents to rich three-dimensional electromagnetic field structures, while establishing a versatile integrated platform for higher-dimensional photonic information processing and emerging material spectroscopies.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Pettine, Tae Gwan Park, Yanhe Lyu, Wangke Yu, John B. Maier, Matthew Yeung, Rujuta Sane, Chun-Chieh Chang, Nuh Gedik, Yijie Shen, Hou-Tong Chen

item.title: Multistable Thermoelectric Josephson Automata
item.description: arXiv:2611.33041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multistable systems can store and process information, yet their elements usually only burn the drive energy. Here, we build an automaton whose elements actively convert heat into electrical power. Heat alone stabilizes the states at zero bias, and each state routes generation and dissipation to different junctions. The elements, gap-asymmetric superconducting tunnel junctions, deliver up to 2.6 pW at either polarity under fixed heating and support a magnetic-field-tunable Josephson current. Two junctions sharing a heated island split the bias hysteretically and, even at zero bias, lock into opposite voltages encoding the sweep direction. With a load and current bias, the automaton accesses states spanning junction polarity combinations, including zero voltage; the magnetic field sets which are available and the bias history selects the occupied one.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Antola, Margherita Cervi, Angelo Greco, Alessandro Braggio, Giorgio De Simoni, Francesco Giazotto

item.title: Signatures of Kitaev quantum spin liquid states in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ revealed by nitrogen-vacancy spin-noise spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.33085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bond-dependent magnetic interactions, strong spin-orbit coupling, and quantum fluctuations in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ make it an archetypical candidate for exotic Kitaev quantum spin liquid (QSL) states. While electronic transport, neutron scattering, optical and tunneling spectroscopies were used to probe global QSL signatures in large scale $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ samples, nanoscale evidence of local QSL behavior via a non-invasive experimental probe is still missing. Here, we use diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin-noise spectroscopy to probe QSL states in {\alpha}-RuCl3 nanoflakes with thicknesses ranging from 8 to 150 nm over a temperature range of 4.3-250 K. Our measurements reveal a pronounced decrease in the NV spin-lattice relaxation time ($T_{1}$) below ~100 K in proximity to the $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ flakes, indicating enhanced GHz-frequency magnetic fluctuations. This temperature scale is consistent with the energy scale associated with Kitaev interactions (~8 meV) and the emergence of low-energy fractionalized excitations. Below 50 K, thicker (> 90 nm) flakes exhibit a distinct bi-exponential $T_{1}$ decay, unlike the single-exponential behavior observed for off-flake and thinner (8 nm) flake measurements, suggesting an increasingly heterogeneous magnetic noise environment. These results establish NV spin-noise spectroscopy as a local, non-invasive probe of low-energy spin dynamics in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ nanoflakes and open a route to testing predicted noise signatures of fractionalized excitations in atomically thin QSL candidates.
item.dc:creator: Jitender Kumar, Sehrish Iqbal, Himani Saraswat, Benjamin Hammons, Tianlin Li, Ariel Smooha, Rupak Timalsina, Arnab K. Pariari, Sy-Hwang Liou, Xia Hong, Markus H\"ucker, Amit Finkler, Abdelghani Laraoui

item.title: A model colloidal gel former for the measurement of inter-particle forces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tracking of particle coordinates in colloidal model systems is an established technique. Recently, an emulsion system has been introduced where not only the coordinates, but also contacts and compressive forces between the droplets can be determined [Dong et al. J. Chem. Phys. 156 214907 (2022). Here we develop this system to control both the density mismatch and refractive index contrast between the emulsion droplets and the solvent. The former is important in minimizing sedimentation due to gravity and the latter is necessary for 3d imaging with confocal microscopy. By mapping our system carefully to computer simulation, we quantify interdroplet forces and packing geometries in depletion gels and probe the relationship between local structure and compressive stress. The simulations also provide ensemble measurements of the attractive part of the force between droplets and related quantities such as the stress tensor. Finally, we implement an improved measure of local stress in our experiments, which can be directly compared with the corresponding quantity in simulations. We find that locally rigid minimum energy clusters are associated with regions of higher stress in the gel network.
item.dc:creator: Rui Cheng, Kristian Thijssen, Abraham Mauleon Amieva, Tanniemola B. Liverpool, Malcolm A. Faers, Robert L. Jack, C. Patrick Royall

item.title: Spin Current Generation Controlled by the N\'{e}el State in a Compensated Ferrimagnet
item.description: arXiv:2507.05618v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Compensated ferrimagnets, which break sublattice and time-reversal symmetries in the ground state, exhibit an isotropic ferromagnet-like spin splitting despite a vanishing net magnetization, in contrast to altermagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting. We investigate how isotropic spin splitting manifests in spin transport by analyzing the spin Seebeck effect and spin pumping in a junction between a compensated ferrimagnet and a normal metal. We show that compensated ferrimagnets generate a sizable spin Seebeck signal, with a sign that can be reversed by switching between the two N\'{e}el states. Furthermore, we demonstrate that spin pumping exhibits a N\'{e}el-state-dependent resonance splitting, which is absent in conventional antiferromagnets. These results identify spin pumping as a natural readout mechanism for compensated ferrimagnets and establish them as promising magnetization-free building blocks for spintronic memory devices.
item.dc:creator: Xin Theng Lee, Takahiro Misawa, Mamoru Matsuo, Takeo Kato

item.title: Voltage-tunable Josephson diode at zero applied field
item.description: arXiv:2508.12056v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a gate-tunable Josephson diode effect in hybrid nanowire junctions consisting of a spin-orbit-coupled semiconductor core coated with epitaxial ferromagnetic insulator and superconductor shells. The wires display a hysteretic superconducting window as a function of axial magnetic field. In the superconducting regime, the devices exhibit nonreciprocal supercurrent transport, with the diode efficiency showing a strong dependence on back-gate voltage. The effect persists at zero applied magnetic field in a remanent magnetization state following a controlled demagnetization procedure. These findings demonstrate a voltage-controlled Josephson diode in a single junction and suggest a route toward probing intrinsically broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries in hybrid materials.
item.dc:creator: Sjoerd Telkamp, Junting Zhao, Saulius Vaitiek\.enas

item.title: Intrinsic spin accumulation in the magnetic spin Hall effect
item.description: arXiv:2509.24719v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The magnetic spin Hall effect is a time-reversal-odd phenomenon in which spin current is induced by the charge current. In the presence of a spin-orbit coupling and/or noncolinear magnetism, however, spin current is not uniquely defined. Instead, we study an intrinsic response of spin to an electric field gradient that describes the spin accumulation at the boundaries of magnetic systems. We derive a generic formula expressed by Bloch wave functions and apply it to a minimal model for representative altermagnets, RuO$_{2}$ and MnF$_{2}$. Our results show that the intrinsic spin accumulation can be nonzero in magnetic insulators in sharp contrast to the magnetic spin Hall conductivity.
item.dc:creator: Atsuo Shitade

item.title: Observation of topological phases without crystalline counterparts
item.description: arXiv:2511.18357v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The center-of-mass position of a nonlinear soliton in a lattice is commonly attributed to the interplay between nonlinearity and lattice confinement. Here, we reveal its geometric origin by establishing an exact relation between the soliton position and an intrinsic Zak phase. Unlike the Zak phase of a linear Bloch band, this intrinsic Zak phase arises from the nonlinear self-consistent band of the lattice reconstructed by the soliton density. We construct a composite periodic function to define this phase and demonstrate that its topological winding during nonlinear Thouless pumping dictates the quantized soliton displacement. Our results establish band geometry as a fundamental descriptor of nonlinear soliton position in a lattice and provide a geometric framework for their topological transport.
item.dc:creator: Mou Yan, Yu-Liang Tao, Yichong Hu, Zhenxing Cui, Jiong-Hao Wang, Gang Chen, Yong Xu

item.title: Floquet Engineering of a Quasiequilibrium Superradiant Phase Transition in Landau Polaritons
item.description: arXiv:2604.08635v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superradiant phase transitions (SRPTs), characterized by photon condensation and macroscopic matter polarization, are forbidden in equilibrium for homogeneous fields by no-go theorems. Here, we show that Floquet driving can circumvent this constraint in a Landau polariton system consisting of a two-dimensional electron gas coupled to a terahertz cavity in a DC magnetic field. An off-resonant AC magnetic field modulates the cyclotron frequency and light--matter coupling strength while leaving the diamagnetic term unchanged, generating an additional DC coupling contribution. This drives the system across a critical threshold into a superradiant phase, characterized by photon condensation and Landau-level polarization in the ground state of the Floquet Hamiltonian. This quasiequilibrium approach offers a route to SRPTs distinct from driven-dissipative schemes.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Hua Wu, Fuyang Tay, Mengqian Che, Andrey Baydin, Junichiro Kono, David Hagenm\"uller

item.title: Micrometer-sized magnonic three-port rectilinear circulator
item.description: arXiv:2606.13540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The development of miniaturized non-reciprocal microwave technologies compatible with integrated circuit architectures remains a critical challenge for modern information technology. Here, we present the first experimental characterization of a micron-sized prototypical magnon circulator. Taking advantage of the chiral excitation of spin-waves via nanowire gratings, we propose an original design of a circulator involving three channels of rectilinear and unidirectional spin-wave beams. We demonstrate via a full 3-port spin-wave spectroscopy a genuine spin-wave circulation between the three ports. The narrow frequency band of operation can be tuned over a broad range of frequencies (2-8 GHz) with both an external field of up to 100 mT, and the dimensions of the grating specifying the wavevectors. This proposed scheme opens up possibilities for architectures of integrated and miniaturized non-reciprocal microwave devices.
item.dc:creator: Kevin S. Weber, Loic Temdie, Vincent Castel, Timmy Reimann, Morris Lindner, Carsten Dubs, Yves Henry, Matthieu Bailleul, Vincent Vlaminck

item.title: Universal scaling of the spin Hall effect
item.description: arXiv:2607.00343v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the spin Hall (SH) effect for the Dirac electrons in terms of the spin and magnetic-moment accumulation coefficients $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy}$. We take short-range nonmagnetic impurities into account within the self-consistent $T$-matrix approximation. Similarly to the universal scaling for the anomalous Hall (AH) effect, we find three distinct regimes by changing the electric conductivity $\sigma^{yy}$; the superclean regime with $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy} \propto \sigma^{yy}$ owing to the skew scattering, moderately dirty regime with almost constant $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy}$, and dirty regime with a scaling relation $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy} \propto (\sigma^{yy})^{0.6}$ whose exponent differs from that of the AH conductivity. Our results construct a unified theory of the SH effect without any ambiguity of spin current.
item.dc:creator: Atsuo Shitade, Naoto Nagaosa

item.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
item.description: arXiv:2607.09511v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their sensitivity to noise is expected to decrease exponentially with increasing separation between the Majoranas, a suppression known as topological protection. Kitaev chains engineered in quantum dot-superconductor arrays provide a tunable platform in which separated Majorana zero modes can emerge at the ends of the chain, even in two-site chains. These minimal-chain modes are known as poor man's Majoranas and retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but have only limited protection. A key outstanding challenge is to move beyond identifying such modes in electrical transport measurements and achieve coherent qubit control in the time domain. Here, we demonstrate a Majorana parity qubit by realizing coherent coupling between two-site Kitaev chains. Since total fermion parity is conserved, the system separates into global even and odd parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both manifolds with equal oscillation frequencies at the Majorana sweet spot, as predicted for isolated Majorana zero modes. We further show that the oscillation frequency and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in close agreement with our model for short, partially protected chains. Our results establish the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit, encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes in minimal Kitaev chains.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo, Antonio Lombardi, Juan D. Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, Vincent P. M. Sietses, Florian J. Bennebroek Evertsz', Pablo Cova Fari\~na, Alberto Bordin, Ghada Badawy, Erik P. A. M. Bakkers, Michael Wimmer, Leo P. Kouwenhoven

item.title: Electrothermal control of spin-reorientation transition in Co/Fe_3GaTe_2 heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2607.15844v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electrical control of magnetic anisotropy in van der Waals (vdWs) magnets is a key step toward reconfigurable two-dimensional spintronics, yet how a conventional metallic ferromagnet competes with a van der Waals magnet across a direct interface has remained largely unexplored. Here we demonstrate reversible thermal and electrothermal control of a spin-reorientation transition in Co/Fe_3GaTe_2 (FGaT) heterostructures. As Joule heating weakens the FGaT anisotropy, the heterostructure switches from an out-of-plane- to an in-plane-dominated state at a reorientation temperature of approximately 311 K, well below the Curie temperature, consistent with an exchange-mediated anisotropy competition between the Co overlayer and FGaT. An electrically driven device shows a closely matching loop evolution within an 80-100 mW power window, reversibly over five measurement cycles, consistent with an electrothermal origin. In a Co-free FGaT device, Kerr microscopy traces the switching to a power-tunable domain nucleation barrier and demonstrates power-thresholded, field-assisted magnetization reversal at a threshold near 15 mW. These results demonstrate electrothermal anisotropy competition as a route to heat-assisted and device-level control of vdWs magnetism.
item.dc:creator: Po-Wei Chen (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan, Department of Physics, The University of Osaka, Toyonaka, Osaka, Japan, Institute of Physics, Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan), Ming-Hsien Hsu (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Cheng-Ying Hsiao (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Ming-Yang Ho (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Masahiro Haze (Institute for Solid State Physics, The University of Tokyo, Kashiwa, Chiba, Japan), Yan-Ru Chu (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Yu-Cheng Shao (National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center, Hsinchu, Taiwan), Po-Chun Chang (Department of Physics, Tamkang University, New Taipei City, Taiwan), Chen-Yu Ou (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Ruei Chen (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Ko-Fan Chen (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Chung-Ting Ke (Institute of Physics, Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan), Chao-Hung Du (Department of Physics, Tamkang University, New Taipei City, Taiwan), Yukio Hasegawa (Institute for Solid State Physics, The University of Tokyo, Kashiwa, Chiba, Japan), Wen-Chin Lin (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan)

item.title: End-State-Controlled Quantum Transport in Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Artificial Quantum Materials
item.description: arXiv:2607.21141v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Artificial quantum materials based on atomically precise graphene nanostructures provide an ideal platform for exploring quantum phenomena arising from localized electronic states. Here, we develop a real-space theoretical framework to elucidate the microscopic origin of interface states in graphene architectures composed of $n$-triangulenes and armchair graphene nanoribbons (AGNRs). By continuously tuning the coupling between graphene building blocks, we reveal the evolution of triangulene zero-energy modes and AGNR end states into compact localized node orbitals at three-arm junctions. For the chiral bipartite junctions considered here, the number and sublattice character of these node orbitals follow a general counting relation, $N_{node,\delta}=|N_{es,t,A(B)}-N_{tri,0,B(A)}|$, where $N_{es,t}$ is the total number of AGNR end states contributed by the three AGNR arms and $N_{tri,0}$ is the number of triangulene zero-energy modes. The resulting node-orbital chirality is determined by the dominant constituent: when $N_{es,t}>N_{tri,0}$, they inherit the sublattice chirality of the AGNR end states ($\delta=A(B)$), whereas for $N_{tri,0}>N_{es,t}$ they inherit that of the triangulene zero-energy modes ($\delta=B(A)$). Using experimentally synthesized triangulene nanographenes as representative examples, we further identify their low-energy zero-mode structure and investigate its manifestation in tunneling transport within an extended Anderson framework. Finally, we demonstrate that these node orbitals can serve as elementary building blocks for constructing artificial graphene nanoribbons with highly tunable flat subbands near the Fermi energy. The resulting compact localized states exhibit controllable degeneracy and strongly anisotropic quantum transport.
item.dc:creator: David M T Kuo

item.title: Circular phonon dichroism in $d$-wave altermagnets
item.description: arXiv:2607.21221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnets, a new class of collinear antiferromagnets, exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting and offer compelling advantages for antiferromagnetic spintronics. However, the magnetic order is intrinsically difficult to read out, which hinders practical applications. We propose finite-momentum circular phonon dichroism as a direct probe that distinguishes the two opposite out-of-plane N\'eel vector configurations in two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnets. Combining Onsager reciprocity with $C_{2z}$ lattice symmetry, we find that the dichroic signal reverses sign when the N\'eel vector is flipped for the in-plane phonon wave vectors. Moreover, a channel-resolved decomposition identifies the circular phonon dichroism originates from the interband coherent transitions. Representative finite-momentum cuts show pronounced dichroic asymmetric ratio, with $|\eta_{\mathrm{CPD}}|=36\%$. Our work reveals that the circular-ultrasound absorption can distinguish the two opposite out-of-plane N\'eel vector configurations of $d$-wave altermagnets.
item.dc:creator: Ding Li, Tao Qin, Jianhui Zhou

item.title: Scanning Gate Microscopy Modulation of Supercurrent in Graphene Josephson Junctions
item.description: arXiv:2607.26689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graphene Josephson junctions (JJs) represent an excellent platform for quantum technologies, thanks to the combination of high carrier mobility, ballistic transport, and gate-tunable critical currents, preserved even under quantizing magnetic fields. Investigating the spatial distribution of supercurrent flow could be crucial for elucidating transport mechanisms and advancing the engineering of these devices. In this work, we employ a scanning gate microscope to investigate supercurrent transport in hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated graphene JJs. We study the supercurrent modulation as a function of tip voltage bias and tip-to-sample distance and provide a complete characterization of the tip-induced modulation. Our experimental results are quantitatively consistent with numerical simulations and pave the way toward local mapping and manipulation of gate-tunable superconducting phenomena with unprecedented spatial resolution.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Villani, Samuele Fracassi, Niccol\`o Traverso Ziani, Maura Sassetti, Matteo Carrega, Vaidotas Miseikis, Camilla Coletti, Fabio Beltram, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sergio Pezzini, Stefan Heun

item.title: The linear stability of electronic Poiseuille flow in two-dimensional materials
item.description: arXiv:2607.29118v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the experimental observation of electronic Poiseuille flow in graphene [J.A. Sulpizio et al. Nature 576, 75 (2019)] we analyze the linear stability of plane-Poiseuille flow of electrons in a two-dimensional material using a modified Orr-Sommerfeld equation. We calculate the critical current needed to make the flow unstable as a function of the experimental parameters and characterize the most favorable situation, that is the one needing the lowest current density, to observe flow instability. We predict the streamwise wavenumber and frequency at which the instability occurs and discuss the difficulties of an experiment aimed at probing this phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Marine Bastida, Alvaro Meseguer, Iacopo Torre

item.title: Spatial exceptional points induced by hyperbolicity in an electrostatic spherical shell
item.description: arXiv:2608.26905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in optics are usually associated with gain and loss or non-reciprocity. In this work we show that a shell with spherical anisotropy supports "spatial EPs" without either. The radial electrostatic problem maps onto a damped oscillator in which the dielectric anisotropy $\varepsilon_r/\varepsilon_t$ is the control parameter. At the EP, the two power-law solutions coalesce spatially and a second, logarithmic solution emerges. Beyond this threshold, the field switches from monotonic decay to spatial oscillation, enabling multiple Fabry-Perot-like resonances. This work reveals how spatial exceptional points modify the optical response of hyperbolic core-shell particles.
item.dc:creator: \'Alvaro Buend\'ia, Marcelo S. Barreiro, Nuno M. R. Peres

item.title: Interferometry reveals spin-singlet fractional quantum Hall edges in graphene
item.description: arXiv:2609.01233v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The edge modes of spin-singlet fractional quantum Hall (FQH) phases are manifestations of multicomponent topological order and SU(2) spin symmetry. An archetype is the spin-unpolarized state at $\nu$=2/3, whose edge is expected to host spatially coexisting yet counter-propagating charge and neutral spin modes. Despite efforts, its edge properties, including spin coherence and spin-charge separation, have remained elusive owing to the difficulty of resolving spins in FQH edge transport. Here, we develop a spin-sensitive probe of graphene FQH edges by using a p-n junction to interface a target FQH state with a probe integer quantum Hall (QH) state of opposite polarity. An Aharonov-Bohm (AB) interferometer forms along the interface, when the target and probe edge channels carry the same spin. We identify the spin-unpolarized and polarized edges of the $\nu$=2/3 states at lower and higher magnetic fields, respectively, through spin-dependent interference. A novel multiparticle AB interference between two electrons of opposite spin emerges from spin-charge separation and recombination on the unpolarized edge, featuring a spin swap. Our results establish edge transport as a probe of spin-singlet topological orders, with implications for parafermion platforms in graphene-superconductor hybrids.
item.dc:creator: R. Ayache, K. Kim, M. Kuiri, Q. Benichou, H. Chakraborti, L. Pugliese, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, H. -S. Sim, P. Roulleau

item.title: Projective representation theory of spin space groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.21289v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin space groups provide the symmetry framework for magnetic crystals with weak spin-orbit coupling, but extracting their physical consequences requires a general theory of irreducible representations. The central difficulty is that spin space groups are represented projectively: their factor systems can render lattice translations noncommuting, induce nonsymmorphic actions in momentum space, and modify the projective structure of little cogroups. These effects lie beyond conventional space-group representation theory. Here, using Mackey's theory of group extensions, we develop a unified constructive framework for all collinear, coplanar, and noncoplanar spin space groups, including antiunitary symmetries and general factor systems. A central result is a canonical decomposition of the relevant factor system $\nu$ into a translational factor $\sigma$, a mixed factor $\gamma$ coupling translations to point-group operations, and a point-group factor $\alpha$. This decomposition makes transparent how ordinary representation theory is modified: $\sigma$ determines the projective translation algebra and the appropriate Brillouin zone, $\gamma$ controls the momentum-space group action and can make it nonsymmorphic, and $\alpha$ contributes to the factor systems of little cogroups. On this basis, we construct all projective irreducible corepresentations by induction over momentum-space orbits. The framework identifies which nonsymmorphic momentum-space symmetries can be realized by spin space groups and how they reconstruct high-symmetry momenta. It reveals Brillouin spaces that are compact flat manifolds, Weyl points of the same chirality locked by projective translation symmetry, and spin space group symmetry-enforced Zak phases as well as Chern insulators. Our results establish the representation-theoretic foundation for systematic studies of weak-spin-orbit-coupled magnetic materials.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Zhang, Peiyuan Wang, Y. X. Zhao

item.title: Enhanced SiV-phonon coupling in dissipation-diluted diamond nanomechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.39271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: Guanhao Huang, Amberly Xie, Chang Jin, Evelyn Hu, Marko Lon\v{c}ar

item.title: Interface Invariants of Rhombohedral Graphene with Layer-dependent Potentials and Couplings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.
item.dc:creator: Yuelong Li

item.title: Hierarchical Deep Research for Physically Grounded System-Level Materials Design
item.description: arXiv:2511.18303v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Designing multicomponent materials systems requires evidence on composition, interfaces, processing and deviceoperation that is scattered across the literature. Language-model research agents can collect this evidence, but their reports are seldom tested against physics. Here we show that Deep Tree of Research, a hierarchical multi-agent system built on locally deployable open-weight language models, ranks first among 47 agents in blinded evaluationacross 27 nanomaterials and device topics. Candidates from local agents outperform those from the best commercial systems on nine of ten first-principles simulation metrics across five design tasks. In a sensing case study, the agent nominated a fluorinated silver-nanoparticle/MXene architecture for the short-chain pollutant perfluoropentanoic acid; after an expert replaced the anchor with an amine, fabricated sensors respond selectively and reproduciblyintap water, consistent with interfacial calculations. Hierarchical research agents can therefore turn dispersed literatureinto experimentally testable materials hypotheses under human supervision.
item.dc:creator: Rui Ding, Rodrigo Pires Ferreira, Yuxin Chen, Junhong Chen

item.title: Light-Matter Interactions Beyond the Electric Dipole Approximation in Extended Systems Without Multipole Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2603.10271v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a general theoretical framework to capture light-matter interactions beyond the electric-dipole approximation, applicable to extended materials interacting with spatially structured electric fields without truncation at finite multipolar order. The approach is based on the Power-Zienau-Woolley (PZW) Hamiltonian for light-matter interactions and a representation of the material Hamiltonian in a basis of maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). We utilize this novel approach to clarify the limitations of the ubiquitous dipole approximation. We consider electric fields with both uniform and non-uniform intensity profiles and a range of ratios of system size to the wavelength of light. We identify the precise conditions under which the dipole approximation breaks down, leading to significant errors in the light-induced dynamics. Contrary to conventional belief, we find that the dipole approximation is robust for uniformly illuminated 1D or 2D materials if light propagates perpendicular to the material. For 3D materials or non-perpendicular illumination, the dipole approximation starts to break down when the wavelength of light becomes comparable to the system size. Furthermore, the dipole approximation fails to capture the light-matter interaction when the material is illuminated partially or non-uniformly. For slowly varying field intensities this failure can be corrected by the finite-order multipolar corrections. However, for fields that vary substantially over the system size, correcting via finite order multipolar terms becomes computationally impractical. In contrast, our approach captures the beyond-dipole light-matter interactions at a computational cost of a standard dipole calculation. This efficiency paves the way for accurate first-principles simulations of spatially-structured light-matter dynamics in nanoscale devices, quantum materials, and interfaces.
item.dc:creator: Rishabh Dora, Roman Korol, Vishal Tiwari, Rahul Chourasiya, Ignacio Franco

item.title: Graphene Josephson diodes from asymmetric disorder
item.description: arXiv:2606.17673v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Josephson diodes are non-reciprocal superconducting devices characterized by different switching currents depending on the current flow direction. They recently attracted considerable theoretical and experimental attention, in view of their possible application as rectifying elements in the field of superconducting electronics, and as probes to investigate symmetry breaking mechanisms in mesoscopic systems. In this work, we show that graphene Josephson junctions provide rectification of supercurrent with an efficiency exceeding 20%. The effect appears applying a mT out-of-plane magnetic field and is enhanced close to the nodes of the Fraunhofer interference pattern. Our findings are consistent with a theoretical model that considers long-range scattering potentials in the junction as the symmetry-breaking mechanism, which yields supercurrent rectification in highly transparent junctions. While graphene stands out as an ultra-clean transmission medium, our work shows that unavoidable residual disorder is sufficient to promote this effect.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Villani, Luca Chirolli, Matteo Carrega, Alessandro Crippa, Elia Strambini, Francesco Giazotto, Vaidotas Miseikis, Camilla Coletti, Fabio Beltram, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Stefan Heun, Sergio Pezzini

item.title: Magnetoelectric flat band induced by a $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ charge density wave in monolayer CrSe$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2606.24494v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the electronic and magnetic properties of the polar $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ charge-density-wave (CDW) phase of CrSe$_2$ using ab initio calculations. The CDW introduces a polar distortion out of the van der Waals plane that couples to the spin-polarized Cr d states resulting in a remarkably flat electronic band exactly at the Fermi level. We provide a microscopic understanding of the origin of the flat band by analyzing in detail the structural reconstruction, the effects of orbital hybridization, crystal-field splittings, spin-orbit coupling and electronic correlations. Our calculations show that due to the polar nature of the CDW distortion, an electric field can act as an external switch to induce the CDW phase, providing a way to manipulate strong correlations in the system.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Savino, M. del Carmen Fuente Santiago, Jan Phillips, Javier Corral Sertal, Adolfo O. Fumega, Santiago Blanco-Canosa, Victor Pardo

item.title: Dynamics of confined acoustic phonon modes in nanocrystalline silicon membranes
item.description: arXiv:2607.14417v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report femtosecond time-resolved measurements of confined acoustic phonons in free-standing nanocrystalline silicon membranes and compare them with the crystalline silicon counterpart. While the latter exhibits well-resolved higher-order modes, a strong suppression of these modes is observed in nanocrystalline samples. The suppression is strongly frequency dependent and becomes more pronounced at shorter phonon wavelengths, consistent with stronger scattering by the nanocrystalline microstructure. Analysis of the phonon lifetimes reveals an additional frequency-dependent scattering mechanism in nanocrystalline silicon, with a scattering rate that scales approximately as $f^2$, where $f$ is the phonon frequency. The measured sound velocity is consistent with previous reports for nanocrystalline silicon and indicates an effective elastic response arising from multiple crystallographic orientations. These results establish coherent phonons as a sensitive probe of microstructure-dependent scattering in nanocrystalline materials and indicate that grain boundaries act as an effective spectral filter for high-frequency acoustic phonons.
